title: Quote Objects
intro: `i"` was just the start: every kind of quote is a text object. `i'` and `a'` work on single-quoted strings, `` i` `` on template literals. If the cursor is before the string on that line, Vim jumps forward to it, so you rarely need to move first. `a` includes the quotes, `i` only what's inside.
summary: Change any string in one move — single, double, or backtick.

exercises.instruction: Switch the theme: with the cursor inside the string, `ci'` then type `light` and press `Esc`.
hints: `ci'` deletes everything between the single quotes and drops you into Insert mode.

exercises.instruction: The cursor is at the start of the line, before the string. `di'` still finds it and empties it.
hints: Quote objects search forward on the current line.

exercises.instruction: Remove the argument completely, quotes included: `da"`.
hints: `i"` would leave the empty quotes behind; `a"` takes them too.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the template literal: `` ci` `` then type `Bye` and press `Esc`.
hints: The backtick is a quote character too.

exercises.instruction: Copy the URL with `yi"`, then move to the end of the line with `$` and paste it before the semicolon with `P`.
hints: `P` pastes before the cursor; `$` puts the cursor on the `;`.

exercises.instruction: Point the request at `/api`: from the start of the line, change the string's contents in one go.
hints: `ci"` jumps forward to the string — no need to move first.

exercises.instruction: Mark the task as `done`, replacing the whole single-quoted string's contents.
